runs.hypothesis: When low-volatility stocks experience a regime transition, their returns reverse in the next period. This is driven by mean-reversion in volatile markets, where low-volatility stocks are overbought during transitions and then underperform as the market stabilizes.

factors.name: LowVolReversal_ZScore
factors.explanation: Computes the z-score of rolling return volatility over 20 days, weighted by a positive percentage change in return over 10 days to capture regime transitions.

factors.name: LowVolReversal_RankGate
factors.explanation: Ranks rolling return volatility over 30 days and gates it by a positive percentage change in return over 15 days to identify regime shifts.

factors.name: LowVolReversal_ConditionalZ
factors.explanation: Uses a conditional gate to switch between 15-day and 30-day volatility z-scores based on a 10-day return increase, capturing regime transitions.

factors.name: LowVolReversal_TsRankGate
factors.explanation: Ranks rolling return volatility over 20 days and gates it by a positive percentage change in return over 10 days to detect regime shifts.

factors.name: LowVolReversal_CorrelationGate
factors.explanation: Combines volatility z-score with a correlation gate between return and volume over 10 days to identify regime transitions.

factors.name: LowVolReversal_VarianceGate
factors.explanation: Measures rolling return variance over 20 days and gates it by a 10-day return increase to capture regime shifts.
